== Who I am ==

My name is Alice C. Munduruca, and I have been a member of the Ubuntu Kernel Team
since Jul. 2025.

=== My Ubuntu story ===

My first time really using Ubuntu was when I helped out with research during university. At that
time, There was a image used for testing SPEC CPU 2017 on Xenial, which was in need of updates for
the architecture simulation software we were using at the time. This allowed me to learn a lot about
linux, debian packaging, and more.  

=== My involvement ===

I help prepare upstream stable updates for the Ubuntu kernel as well as CVE backports.

=== Endorsements ===

-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----

=== Vinicius Peixoto (vpeixoto) ===

I have worked with Alice since she joined Canonical in 2025. From my
experience, she has always been very sharp and quick-witted, going through the
kernel team ramp-up process in record time; besides the kernel cranking, she
has also put out a huge amount of CVE fix backports (several of which were
non-trivial) and developed a bespoke tool for validating and automating a large
part of that process, as well as prepared several stable release updates for
generic kernels.

I have reviewed and sponsored several of her kernels, all of which were
prepared diligently and in a timely manner, and found no issues with the vast
majority of them. The only time one of her cranks had to be redone was due to
an emergency respin that was pushed in between her starting and finishing the
crank (essentially just unfortunate timing), and she fixed the issue very
swiftly. She is also very thorough with her review of test results (having even
gone as far as sending patches upstream to fix faulty tests in our RT suite)
and never hesitates to reach out and ask questions on the rare occasion that
she hits an issue that she can't solve herself.

I have full confidence in giving her my endorsement.

=== Edoardo Canepa (ecanepa) ===

I’ve had the opportunity to review several kernels that Alice uploaded, and they were consistently flawless and prepared with the utmost care. I’ve also reviewed some of her stable submissions, which were thoughtful and well considered, and she was always quick and precise in addressing my questions.

Given the relatively short time since she joined, she has already made meaningful contributions by quickly learning and following the various processes, as well as improving them and developing tools to automate parts of the workflow and make them more efficient.

Based on these experiences, I’m confident in her ability to handle kernel uploads carefully and responsibly.
